de5_life.topic: Curtis Yarvin: family, schooling, early career (documented and own account)

claims.text: Yarvin's father was a US foreign service officer; the family was posted to Portugal, Cyprus and the Dominican Republic and earlier lived in Fairfax County, Virginia; his mother, a Protestant from Westchester County, later joined the civil service; parents met at Brown in the mid-1960s; paternal grandparents were Jewish American communists

Yarvin skipped grades, was 11 in ninth grade, a 12-year-old sophomore at a public high school in Columbia, Maryland; at 15 entered Johns Hopkins' Study of Mathematically Precocious Youth and a year later transferred to Brown as a legacy admission; began a CS PhD at Berkeley and left after about a year and a half
Yarvin worked at a mobile software company founded in 1996 as Libris, later Unwired Planet then Phone.com; after the dot-com crash a buyout gave him 'a few hundred thousand dollars'
Yarvin: 'Hoppe opened a kind of door to the pre-revolutionary world for me'

Born 1973 to a liberal, secular family (Tait 2019; Pein 2018); father a diplomat in Nicosia per Yarvin (Raskin interview); Wilde Lake High School 1988 cited to his own 2011 post; Brown 1992; Berkeley CS PhD left after ~1.5 years (Tait; Siegel); sometimes homeschooled by his mother, skipped three grades (Kofman, New Yorker, 2 June 2025)
In the NYT interview (Jan 2025) Yarvin said his parents were career federal civil servants; born 1973 to a diplomat father whose parents were Jewish American communists and a Protestant mother

de5_urbit.topic: Urbit and Tlon: founding, Thiel/Founders Fund money, 2019 exit, 2024-25 return

claims.text: Founders Fund (Thiel) and Andreessen Horowitz invested $1.1 million in Tlon, per Corey Pein, Live Work Work Work Die (2018); first public Urbit code release January 2010 (Yarvin's 13 Jan 2010 post); Yarvin left Tlon in 2019; The Point (Sept 2022) estimated active users at 'a few thousand'
Yarvin returned to a leadership role at Urbit in 2024 as an informal 'wartime C.E.O.'; several top employees resigned in protest (ARTnews 29 Aug 2024; Kofman, New Yorker 2025)
Yarvin, who had left Urbit in January 2019, announced a return 'in a big way' at a public meeting in August 2024; his 2019 departure post was titled 'A Founder's Farewell'

By July 2025 the Urbit Foundation had had four executive directors in about a year; Executive Director Ryan Kneer fired Yarvin from the board, while Yarvin lobbied the other two board members to fire Kneer; Kneer appealed to galaxy holders

July 2025: a newsletter writer who holds Urbit address space reported Yarvin acting as executive director 'by fiat', quoting him calling it 'real Roman times', and reported (terms unknown) a $4M a16z investment for address space earlier in 2025; the Galactic Senate vote outcome was unreported

de5_public.topic: Yarvin's public years: Vance 2021 remark and later engagement

claims.text: Vance on Jack Murphy Live (2021): 'There's this guy, Curtis Yarvin. Who's written about some of these things.' ... 'I'm sympathetic to that project. But another option is that we should just seize the administrative state for our own purposes.'

Vance in a 2021 podcast: 'fire every single mid-level bureaucrat, every civil servant in the administrative state'; 'Replace them with our people'; 'The chief justice has made his ruling. Now let him enforce it.'
The Vance remark dates to September 2021 on a conservative podcast
Yarvin was 'an informal guest of honor' at the 'Coronation Ball', an inaugural gala hosted by Passage Press (Politico's description)
Yarvin: 'I [recently] had lunch with Mike Anton at a coffee shop across the street from the State Department'
Yarvin: 'I've interacted with Vance once since the election. I bumped into him at a party'; Vance greeted him 'Yarvin, you reactionary fascist' (Yarvin's account)
Yarvin on influence: 'how I measure my influence is that I try not to'; the New Right 'is still a vanguard'; people who read him in middle school 'are getting jobs more easily'
Asked if a figure was Peter Thiel, Yarvin: 'No, no, no, this is someone you've never heard of'; Yarvin: 'America just has a really shitty government and needs a new government'

Yarvin debated Danielle Allen at Harvard's Faculty Club on 5 May 2025; organized by Passage Publishing with the John Adams Society; not sanctioned by Harvard; ~80 attendees; moderator David A. Vega; Yarvin called Harvard 'an essentially oligarchic institution'; Allen: 'The divergence is in whether the question is regime change to unaccountable CEO monarchs'
Yale Federalist Society hosted 'For-Profit Governance (Curtis Yarvin v. Garett Jones)' on 8 October 2025
Yale Political Union debate on Tuesday 7 October 2025: Yarvin v. Jed Rubenfeld on 'end the democratic experiment' (no vote total found)

In an October 2025 Gray Mirror post Yarvin wrote he must 'start thinking realistically about how to flee the country' (later edited to a 'plan B for 2029'); earlier in 2025 he wrote the administration would 'wither and eventually dissipate' unless it grew more extreme
Andreessen called Yarvin a 'good friend'; Vance follows him on X

The May 2021 Anton–Yarvin conversation was recorded for the Claremont Institute's The American Mind podcast, ostensibly about Anton's 2020 book The Stakes; Power Line argued the Guardian's account did not match the recording

Per the Guardian (Wilson, 21 Dec 2024) as relayed, in the May 2021 conversation Yarvin called the idea of becoming 'a Caesar' 'manifestly absurd' and discussed a president declaring a state of emergency in the inaugural address

Unqualified Reservations began 2007, largely stopped 2013; in April 2016 Yarvin said it had 'completed its mission' (Tait 2019); Gray Mirror began on Substack in 2020; his wife Jennifer Kollmer died in 2021 (his post of 7 April 2021); married Kristine Militello in 2024 (The Information); Bregman's November 2025 Reith Lecture called him 'neofascist'

Strange Loop rescinded Yarvin's invitation for 2015; LambdaConf 2016 (Boulder) kept him as a speaker on Urbit after speakers and sponsors withdrew and a petition objected; organizer John A. De Goes said they had not known his views
After Trump took office, reports circulated that Yarvin was secretly advising Steve Bannon; 'Yarvin denied the rumors, sometimes playfully and at other times strenuously'

Thiel attended Yarvin's late-February 2020 Los Angeles podcast appearance; Yarvin 'went silent' in 2014 after seven years of blogging; Siegel describes his proposed regime change as one 'achieved without any violence or even activism'
Passage Publishing sells Yarvin's Gray Mirror: Fascicle I, Disturbance (2022), Unqualified Reservations Vol. I and Vol. 2

Gray Mirror describes itself as 'A portal to the next regime', 'with tens of thousands of subscribers', by Curtis Yarvin 'once known as Mencius Moldbug'; the book project Gray Mirror of the Nihilist Prince offers an 'ex nihilo vision of governance'

Yarvin was a 'convidado de honra' (guest of honour) at the national convention launching Partido Missão, organized by MBL, in São Paulo (late November 2025); in a roughly six-minute speech he argued against racial quotas and US-imported racial-equality ideas
Berliner Zeitung interview (19 Oct 2025): Yarvin wished Trump were far more energetic; he advocates a CEO-led quasi-monarchy
At HowTheLightGetsIn in London (Sept 2025), interviewed by Alastair Campbell, Yarvin called the rule of law a 'polite fiction' for the rule of men
German public broadcaster 3sat's Kulturzeit ran a segment on Yarvin on 19 January 2026

de5_kofman.topic: Kofman's New Yorker profile (2 June 2025) via Nueva Sociedad translation

claims.text: Partly homeschooled by his mother, skipped three grades, entered high school at 12 after the family moved to Columbia, Maryland; father Herbert held a philosophy PhD before becoming a diplomat; family lived in the Dominican Republic and Cyprus

Graduated from Brown at 18; left Berkeley's CS PhD after about a year and a half; helped design an early mobile browser at the company later called Phone.com; its IPO brought him roughly $1 million (Kofman), which funded his self-directed study
TechCrunch linked the Moldbug pseudonym to Yarvin in 2013; the 2008 'open letter' ran about 120,000 words and called for a 'CEO-monarch'

Kofman: Tlon founded 2013, Urbit reportedly with about $30 million in investment; Yarvin left in 2019, returned in 2024 as 'wartime CEO' after which several key employees resigned; in February 2025 he sought funding again from Andreessen Horowitz

Kofman: Thiel and Balaji Srinivasan befriended Yarvin after reading his blog; Founders Fund invested in Tlon; Yarvin claimed he watched an election at Thiel's house and 'advised' Thiel; Yarvin met Vance in 2015 through Thiel; Vance later followed him on X

Kofman: an anonymous DOGE adviser told the Washington Post everyone designing policy had read him; Yarvin complained DOGE had too much libertarian DNA and called his own influence counterfeit currency until his preferred revolution happened
